verdict: Revenue rose 6% on strong demand for sleep devices and masks, and a $62M gain on selling MatrixCare lifted net income 20% to $418M.

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: Operating cash flow of $422M minus spending on property and equipment

segments.name: Sleep Devices
segments.note: Machines that treat sleep apnea and related breathing problems.

segments.name: Masks and other
segments.note: Masks and accessories used with the devices.

segments.name: Residential Care Software
segments.note: Software for home-health and care providers (Brightree and MEDIFOX DAN); reported sales fell because the MatrixCare business was sold, while the remaining businesses grew 8%.

segments.name: Life Support Devices
segments.note: Ventilators and life-support devices — now a very small line as the business winds down.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing new sleep and breathing devices and software.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling products, running the company, and amortization of acquired intangibles (spreading the cost of past acquisitions).

takeaways.title: Revenue rose to $1.41B
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 6% to $1.41B, driven by sleep devices (+9% to $716M) and masks and other products (+10% to $540M).

takeaways.title: A business sale boosted profit
takeaways.text: Other income includes a $62M gain on selling the MatrixCare software business. Without it, operating income of $453M was up just 1% from a year earlier.

takeaways.title: Net income rose 20%
takeaways.text: Net income was $418M, up from $349M a year earlier, and the company returned $1.0B to shareholders in the quarter through dividends and buybacks, helped by the MatrixCare sale proceeds.

oneTimers: Other income includes a $62M gain on the divestment of the MatrixCare subsidiary, completed in the quarter.
footerNote: Fiscal year ends June 30, so the quarter ended September 30, 2026 is the first quarter of fiscal 2027. Other income of $86M includes the $62M MatrixCare divestment gain, $16M of net interest income, and smaller gains on equity investments. Segment figures are the product totals from the release's revenue-by-product table; totals may not add in the release due to rounding, and here they sum exactly to revenue in whole millions.
follow100Note: Segment percentages sum to 99.99 due to rounding to two decimal places.
